closed_jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Integrated Producer to build and scale OpenAI’s creative production capabilities both internally and with trusted vendors. You will establish production strategy, ensure flawless campaign execution, and manage budgets across the marketing organization.

The ideal candidate has a proven track record of leading large-scale productions and building processes that enable iconic creative work. You will also be responsible for growing and leading a high-performing production team to support OpenAI’s ambitious global growth goals.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead Integrated Campaign Strategy: Work closely with Strategy, Business, Product, and Operations teams to develop and execute marketing campaigns that align with business objectives across paid, owned, and earned channels.

  • Drive Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with teams across Product, Product Marketing, Business Marketing, Communications, Global Affairs, and Creative to ensure cohesive, impactful campaigns.

  • Manage End-to-End Campaign Execution: Own the planning, execution, and post-launch analysis of integrated campaigns — from brief and conceptual development through launch and optimization.

  • Establish Production Processes: Build scalable processes and best practices that ensure seamless execution of integrated campaigns globally.

  • Vendor and Budget Management: Identify, onboard, and manage production vendors and agencies while maintaining strong budget stewardship.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of experience in marketing and advertising, including at least 3 years focused on integrated or campaign-driven roles. Prior experience at both agencies and in-house marketing teams is a plus.

  • Proven Success Managing Cross-Channel Campaigns: Demonstrated ability to lead campaigns across digital, social, email, paid media, and events. Strong understanding of content marketing, customer journey mapping, and lead generation.

  • Expertise Across Traditional and Digital Marketing: Proficiency in TV, OOH, social media, content, and event production.

  • Strong Project Management Skills: Track record of managing multiple priorities, meeting deadlines, and driving results with a data-driven approach using analytics tools to inform strategy.

  • Excellent Communication and Influence: Ability to collaborate across disciplines and present to executive audiences; adept at tailoring messaging for diverse audiences.

  • Agility and Adaptability: Comfort working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and ability to pivot strategies based on evolving market needs.

Nice to have:

  • A creative and strategic approach to campaign development.

  • Confidence leading cross-functional teams and managing senior stakeholders.

  • A passion for storytelling and connecting audiences to brand narratives.

  • A test-and-learn mindset, focused on continuous optimization.

  • Familiarity with AI technologies and emerging marketing trends.

closed_jobs.title: IC Agentic Engineering Manager - Stargate
closed_jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Stargate Infrastructure team is building and operating the systems that power next-generation AI workloads at massive scale. This includes deploying and managing clusters, networks, and data center infrastructure across first-party and partner environments.

As the scale and complexity of these systems grow, we are investing in agentic systems and intelligent automation to improve how infrastructure is deployed, operated, and debugged. This team focuses on applying AI-driven approaches to real-world infrastructure workflows—enabling faster execution, higher reliability, and scalable operations.

About the Role

We are seeking an IC Agentic Engineering Manager to lead the development and application of agent-based systems for infrastructure delivery and operations within Stargate.

This is a player-coach role: you will contribute directly to system design and implementation while leading a small team. You will focus on applying agentic systems to infrastructure workflows such as deployment orchestration, system bring-up, issue triage, debugging, and capacity management.

This role is not focused on building general-purpose agent platforms. Instead, it is centered on applying agentic systems to solve concrete infrastructure problems, working closely with hardware, networking, and cluster teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and build agent-based systems to support infrastructure deployment and operations

  • Identify high-impact opportunities to apply agents across workflows such as:

    • cluster bring-up and deployment readiness

    • incident triage and root cause analysis

    • system validation and health monitoring

    • capacity management and operational decision-making

  • Lead a small team while contributing directly as an IC across system design, development, and integration

  • Partner with infrastructure, hardware, and networking teams to integrate agentic systems into production workflows

  • Develop systems that leverage telemetry, logs, and system signals to enable closed-loop automation

  • Define evaluation frameworks to measure system effectiveness, reliability, and operational impact

  • Drive iteration from prototype to production, ensuring robustness and scalability

Qualifications

  • Strong software engineering background in distributed systems, infrastructure, or platform engineering

  • Experience building production automation systems or data-driven operational tooling

  • Experience applying AI, ML, or agent-based approaches to real-world systems or workflows

  • Ability to operate as a hands-on IC while leading a small team

  • Experience working cross-functionally with infrastructure, hardware, or systems teams

  • Strong problem-solving skills in complex, ambiguous environments

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with LLM-based systems, agents, or autonomous workflows

  • Background in infrastructure operations, SRE, or large-scale system deployment

  • Experience working on cluster bring-up, debugging, or data center infrastructure systems

  • Familiarity with telemetry, monitoring systems, and observability pipelines

closed_jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI's mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. If you're passionate about doing significant and unique work in the legal and compliance field, this team is for you. The team comprises professionals from diverse fields, including technology, AI, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax law, regulatory, and litigation.

About the Role

As a member of our Security Legal team, you will be responsible for managing and evolving OpenAI’s sanctions compliance program, from developing an overall compliance strategy, mapping out screening architecture and workflow designs, and working cross functionally with colleagues on monitoring, metrics, and continuous improvement. You will manage sanctions compliance policy and strategy for one of the most closely watched and globally impactful technology platforms in the world, and have real ownership and the chance to develop systems that scale globally as the company and our technology continues to evolve. You’ll also collaborate on adjacent trade compliance and security issues.

This role can be hybrid or remote and based in San Francisco, Washington, D.C., New York, or Seattle. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role you will:

  • Advise cross-functional teams on compliance and legal requirements applicable to OpenAI’s products and services under U.S. and international sanctions regimes.

  • Develop sanctions compliance strategies and processes at a global scale for a frontier AI company operating across jurisdictions and products.

  • Partner closely with cross-functional teams across Finance, Integrity, GRC, and Engineering to implement sanctions screening and controls that are deeply embedded into business workflows.

  • Own compliance documentation and reporting, including policies, standards, dashboards, metrics, and escalation frameworks to enable rapid monitoring, assessment, and improvement of compliance processes

  • Work with cross-functional teams to deeply understand and integrate compliance systems and tools, ensuring compliance checks are seamless, reliable, and adaptable as OpenAI evolves.

  • Lead ongoing reviews and risk assessments to ensure the continued effectiveness of our compliance controls and processes.

  • Manage and coordinate vendors and other third parties who support OpenAI’s compliance operations.

  • Assist in the development of trade compliance training materials for our cross-functional partners and business teams.

  • Explore and deploy AI tools to enhance and streamline OpenAI’s trade compliance efforts.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience in the trade compliance field, including developing and implementing trade compliance programs at a large, technology-focused company.

  • Hold a J.D. from an accredited law school and maintain an active license to practice law, in good standing, in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

  • Bring a sophisticated understanding of how US and international sanctions laws apply to multinational US companies.

  • Have successfully embedded comprehensive compliance programs and incorporated compliance processes into complex business workflows without slowing innovation.

  • Enjoy learning new systems and becoming the go-to expert in the systems and technical tools required for your job.

  • Are highly skilled at program management, including organizing complex systems, tasks, processes, and documentation.

  • Communicate in a way that builds trust with cross-functional teams, from engineers to business leaders.

  • Have a strong sense of ownership, are inquisitive and enthusiastic about technology, enjoy being continually challenged, and can demonstrate sound judgment in ambiguous situations.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

About the Role

As a Technical Deployment Lead Manager (TDL Manager) in the FDE team, you will build and lead TDLs through high-stakes, ambiguous customer deployments and own technical and business value outcomes end to end. You’ll grow a team that can operate under pressure and help OpenAI learn from the field.

You will lead TDLs who translate business outcomes into technical delivery plans, run day-to-day execution across FDEs, Researchers, and Customer Engineers, and partner with customer teams to ensure delivery supports their goals. You will set the bar on scope, sequencing, risk management, and communication. When deployments drift or stakes spike, you will step in to reset the plan, unblock teams, and protect customer trust.

Your decisions will influence how OpenAI is trusted by the customers closest to our deployment work. Your success will be measured by how consistently your team ships, how clearly you deliver signal to Research and Product, and how durable your team and delivery model prove to be.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel of approximately 25% is required.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead and grow a team of TDLs delivering production systems with frontier models

  • Own end-to-end delivery outcomes through clarity, speed, tight coordination, and technical quality

  • Codify what works into tools, playbooks, and roadmap inputs that create leverage

  • Notice early indicators and raise them with urgency, whether in product behavior, customer environments, or delivery practices

  • Use judgement to distinguish what requires action and what does not

  • Set a high bar for TDL performance and support each person’s growth through direct, actionable feedback

  • Define how we staff and support field teams that can scale without added complexity

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Bring 8+ years of customer-facing technical delivery leadership, including 2+ years managing high-performing technical delivery, program management, or customer engineering teams.

  • Have led high-pressure technical projects from prototype to production.

  • Simplify complex work and make fast, sound decisions under pressure.

  • Elevate team performance through clarity, not process.

  • Operate with urgency in ambiguous or evolving environments.

  • Build deep trust with your team by modeling calm, focus, and judgment when it matters most.

  • Have built and scaled an operating model for delivery: staffing, cadence, artifacts, risk management, and clear ownership across teams.

closed_jobs.title: Travel Operations Lead
closed_jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Procurement organization enables our mission by ensuring every dollar is spent responsibly, compliantly, and efficiently. As a key part of this function, this role reports to the Head of Travel & Expense (T&E) and partners closely with Procurement Operations, Accounting, Finance, and business stakeholders to own and scale the company's global Events strategy, operations, and compliance.

About the Role

We are looking for a Travel Operations Lead to own and mature the operating model behind OpenAI's executive and employee travel programs. This role will be hands-on in executive travel support while also building the policies, supplier relationships, data, systems, and AI-enabled workflows that allow the program to scale with speed, confidentiality, safety, and control.

This person will oversee high-touch executive travel support, including complex commercial travel globally; manage travel agency and supplier performance; own the executive travel policy; and partner with Executive Business Partners to ensure travelers receive timely, high-quality support. The role will also own core employee travel operations, TMC support, on-the-road escalation management, executive travel reporting for tax and compliance purposes, and guest T&E programs.

What we're looking for:

We are looking for someone who understands the nuance of the travel industry and can operate at scale while continuously improving the system. This person will be hands-on in executive travel support and will own the policy, operation, supplier relationships, and support model that enable safe, efficient, and high-quality travel.

The right person will bring strong operational judgment, high attention to detail, and the ability to adjust policies, programs, and tools as OpenAI scales. They will also bring a practical vision for AI and agentic enablement across the travel support ecosystem, knowing where AI can reduce manual work, where human review matters, and how to build trust in new ways of working.

You bring:

  • 7+ years of experience in travel, executive operations, expense, corporate cards, sourcing, finance operations, or a related T&E role.

  • High AI fluency, with demonstrated ability to use AI tools to improve how work gets done, reduce manual effort, strengthen analysis, improve documentation, and create scalable operating leverage.

  • Strong understanding of how the in-trip experience is affected by disruptions, destination risk, traveler context, supplier performance, policy design, booking quality, and support responsiveness.

  • Ability to improve operational processes through better data, automation, workflow design, and exception-based ways of working.

  • Strong systems understanding, with the ability to understand how data flows across procurement, travel, finance, tax, card, and reporting platforms.

  • High attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership for data accuracy, completeness, confidentiality, and consistency.

  • Ability to identify patterns in operational issues and translate them into better processes, standards, controls, and system improvements.

  • Practical judgment around AI adoption, including where automation can accelerate work, where human review matters, and how to build trust with travelers and cross-functional partners.

  • Comfort working across HR, Finance, Accounting, Procurement Operations, Tax, Legal, Security, Executive Business Partners, and business stakeholders.

  • Clear communication skills and the ability to explain process requirements in a practical, enablement-focused way.

  • Sound judgment when handling confidential executive travel information, sensitive traveler data, guest information, and supplier performance concerns.

  • Ability to operate in ambiguity, bring structure to evolving processes, and raise the bar as volume and complexity increase.

Workplace & Location

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the executive travel operating model, including support workflows, escalation paths, SLA management, policy ownership, supplier coordination, and program governance.

  • Lead high-touch executive travel support including complex commercial travel globally, balancing speed, confidentiality, safety, and experience.

  • Manage the procurement process for executive travel, including supplier engagement, service expectations, documentation, spend visibility, and compliance with procurement and finance requirements.

  • Own and continuously improve the executive travel policy, translating edge cases into clear standards, practical guardrails, and scalable approval paths.

  • Partner with Executive Business Partners to optimize support, improve satisfaction, clarify handoffs, and ensure executives and travelers can travel safely and effectively.

  • Oversee employee travel support related to TMC service delivery, on-the-road support, disruption management, traveler enablement, and recurring issue resolution.

  • Own travel agency management for Navan and related program operations, including SLAs, KPIs, escalations, roadmap input, operational reviews, and continuous improvement.

  • Manage the Guest T&E program for new hires, candidates, and other business guests, creating scalable rules, support workflows, payment paths, and exception handling.

  • Build reporting and data routines for executive travel, tax, compliance, supplier performance, traveler experience, support volume, and operational risk.

  • Use AI tools to improve travel support workflows, documentation, triage, analytics, policy interpretation, exception routing, and recurring issue detection.

  • Partner cross-functionally with HR, Finance, Accounting, Procurement Operations, Tax, Legal, Security, Executive Business Partners, Recruiting, and business stakeholders.

  • Build clear documentation, SOPs, program standards, and operating rhythms that make travel support easier, more consistent, and more transparent.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have worked on scaled travel programs and understand how global travel operations, supplier performance, policy, traveler experience, and data connect.

  • Have experience in high-touch, highly confidential, and fast-changing environments where judgment, discretion, and service quality matter.

  • Can set up program rules that scale with volume and complexity while preserving room for practical exception handling.

  • Understand how disruptions, risk, routing, supplier behavior, traveler profiles, and support timing affect trip outcomes.

  • Enjoy turning operational complexity into clear standards, better workflows, stronger controls, and smarter systems.

  • Are already using AI tools to improve quality, speed, analysis, documentation, traveler support, or decision support.

  • Can balance hands-on support with strategic program ownership and cross-functional influence.

  • Bring an ownership mindset and are comfortable being accountable for sensitive, visible, and operationally complex work.

Compensation Range: $216K - $240K USD

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. closed_jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance ensures the organization is commercially, operationally, and structurally set up to deliver on OpenAI’s mission at global scale.

The Strategic Sourcing team partners with Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, and Finance to ensure OpenAI acquires the critical external technology, platforms, and services needed to launch new products, operate safely, and monetize globally with speed, resilience, and commercial discipline.

This role is based in San Francisco (hybrid, 3 days/week in office).

About the Role

We are hiring a Strategic Sourcing Lead (Ads & Consumer Verticals) to manage the commercial execution and vendor strategy across this expanding footprint.

This role will serve as the day-to-day commercial owner for a growing portfolio of vendors across brand safety, measurement and attribution, fraud prevention and invalid traffic detection technologies, health and finance applications, enabling OpenAI to launch new capabilities, enter new markets, and scale monetization without accumulating excessive cost, risk, or operational fragility.

You will report to the Technology Strategic Sourcing Lead (Product Ecosystem & Monetization) and work closely with Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Growth, and Finance leaders to translate product roadmaps into scalable, defensible vendor strategies.

In this role, you will:

  • Own sourcing and commercial strategy across OpenAI’s ads technology stack and consumer verticals with a focus on health and finance.

  • Run high-velocity, high-complexity deals end-to-end: from vendor strategy and RFPs through negotiation, security review, contracting, and go-live.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure external vendors can support new product launches without blocking delivery or increasing risk.

  • Build and manage a multi-vendor ads technology ecosystem, health and personal finance focussed tools, to support revenue growth, engagement, and cost optimization.

  • Structure contracts and pricing models that preserve optionality, support rapid scaling, and minimize long-term lock-in and switching costs.

  • Coordinate Security, Legal, and Privacy reviews, especially for regulated data flows (health, personal financial) and high-risk vendors.

  • Own vendor lifecycle management: onboarding, ramp-ups, SLA enforcement, renewals, and re-competitions as OpenAI’s volumes and risk profile evolve.

  • Act as the control plane between fast-moving product teams and external dependencies, ensuring speed without sacrificing governance, compliance, or economics.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 6+ years of experience leading technology partnerships, sourcing, or commercial negotiations in a high-growth, product-driven environment.

  • Have demonstrated strong cross-functional leadership and are able to align Product, Engineering, Legal, Security, and Finance around complex, high-stakes decisions.

  • Are comfortable operating in regulated or high-risk domains (personal financial, health, payments, identity, data etc).

  • Have a track record of negotiating commercial, technical, and data-driven agreements with technology vendors.

  • Enjoy moving quickly in ambiguity while maintaining commercial discipline, compliance, and risk awareness.

  • Have strong analytical skills to evaluate pricing models, volume ramps, and vendor risk in the context of revenue and product growth.

  • Bring an ownership mindset—you independently drive deals, resolve blockers, and close outcomes that materially impact product launches and revenue.

  • Have a desire to accelerate OpenAI’s mission by enabling better vendor partnerships, faster launches, and more effective execution at scale.

closed_jobs.title: Manager, Occupancy Planning Operations
closed_jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Real Estate and Workplace team at OpenAI is pivotal in crafting and maintaining the physical environments that fuel our innovation and growth. This team ensures our facilities align with our dynamic business objectives. We manage daily operations, optimize workspace designs, and manage leasing and planning for our real estate portfolio. With a strong focus on sustainability and efficiency, the team works closely with internal stakeholders and external partners to create spaces that not only reflect our brand's identity and culture but also enhance employee productivity and well-being. Joining this team means being at the heart of shaping the environments that inspire our technological advancements and support our mission.

About the Role

As a member of the Real Estate & Workplace team, you will own the end-to-end execution of employee and team moves and the program management of our CAFM platform. You will translate approved occupancy strategies into safe, accurate, low-disruption moves—from intake, scenario validation, and sequencing through communications, vendor coordination, day-of execution, and post-move stabilization. In parallel, you will serve as the business program lead for CAFM, driving its roadmap, data governance, integrations, release management, and adoption so workplace teams operate from reliable space and occupancy data.

This is an individual contributor role based in San Francisco, CA, operating on a hybrid model with three office days per week. Relocation assistance is available to new hires. Success in this role is measured by predictable move delivery, employee readiness, cost and schedule control, accurate CAFM data, strong user adoption, and continuous improvement.

In this role you will:

Move Planning & Execution

  • Lead concurrent office moves, restacks, and phased relocations from approved scope through move-day execution, stabilization, and closeout.

  • Build integrated move plans covering schedules, budgets, dependencies, seating, IT/AV, security, furniture, facilities, accessibility, communications, and contingencies.

  • Translate business requirements and stacking plans into move waves; lead readiness reviews, issue resolution, and post-move retrospectives.

Cross-Functional & Vendor Leadership

  • Establish clear responsibilities, decision-making processes, and escalation paths across business leaders, People, IT, Security, Facilities, Communications, and Finance.

  • Manage move vendors and workplace service providers, including scope, schedules, deliverables, quality, safety, and costs.

  • Communicate plans, risks, and decisions to employees and executives while minimizing business disruption.

Move Operations & Performance

  • Develop scalable move playbooks, RACI models, readiness checklists, cutover plans, and service standards.

  • Maintain risk and issue logs, change control, budget tracking, and governance across the move portfolio.

  • Track KPIs—including readiness, move accuracy, downtime, employee experience, and cost—to improve future execution.

CAFM Program Management

  • Own the CAFM roadmap, governance, budget, vendor performance, and success measures.

  • Translate workplace workflows into system requirements and releases; oversee configuration, testing, launch readiness, and change control.

  • Establish standards for floorplans, occupancy, employee assignments, and move data, maintaining CAFM as the system of record throughout the move lifecycle.

  • Drive adoption through documentation, training, support, and integrations with HRIS, ITSM, access control, reservations, and analytics.

You’ll might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 5-8+ years of experience in workplace operations, move management, space and occupancy planning, or corporate real estate in a dynamic, high-growth environment.

  • Demonstrated success leading concurrent, complex office moves and relocations end to end, including schedule, budget, vendor, communications, cutover, risk, and stabilization ownership.

  • Hands-on experience serving as a business owner, product or program manager, or administrator for CAFM/IWMS platforms such as OfficeSpace, including requirements, UAT, data governance, integrations, and adoption.

  • Strong program management, analytical, and executive communication skills; able to manage budgets, vendors, RAID and change control, and KPIs using Google Workspace, Tableau, and related reporting tools.
